Here is the eulogy of Clementa Pinckney that the President delivered last Friday (6/26/15). Watching this, I couldn't help but wonder what Hitch's take would have been. After broadcasting the eulogy, CNN cut to Don Lemon and Van Jones outside, where the two (black) men were as speechless as you'll ever find reporters/political commentators. That scene reminded me of many others which Hitchens seemed to apt to recall in analyzing the reactions of others.

I'll weigh in below in the comments, leaving you all the choice to voat on the prompt and my response separately.

Edit - Here is (most of) the analysis of Lemon and Jones following the eulogy.

Edit 2 - I realize that one of the defining characteristics of Hitch is that you could never be 100% sure what he'd say about any given issue. However, when it comes to honest intellectual evaluation of an important and controversial issue, I don't think it's unreasonable to frame the discussion in this way. We can't be sure what Hitch would have said, but the exercise of trying to be critical of something in the way he would have is something we can all benefit from.
What would Hitchens have said about Pres. Obama's eulogy for Clementa Pinckney in Charleston?

One of the things that stood out to me the most was how obvious the President was in his shifting between his standard speaking voice and his moments of slang and southern accent. I realize that he has a background as a community organizer, and that in this culture, a black man expecting to command respect has to speak in a certain way, but my impression was that he was pandering to the black crowd, not that he was "letting his true self shine through."

I am the sort of person that hates when a person appeals to faith in a speech, and I also despise when someone over-emphasizes racial issues. The President did both of those things, and advocated stronger gun control, yet I found myself moved by his speech. I felt myself being lulled into a place of refusal to criticize because of the emotion of the crowd and the skill Mr. Obama has as an orator. For those reasons, I'm skeptical of my own feelings towards the speech, which is why I call upon you all who share an appreciation of skepticism and contrarianism to help me see through the fog that good speech writing and delivery can create.
